title: Earthrise
caption: Earthrise — the first photograph of our planet from the Moon, drawn entirely from the opening of Genesis that the Apollo 8 crew read aloud from lunar orbit on Christmas Eve 1968.
source: Genesis 1–11, King James Version (1611), public domain; the Apollo 8 crew read Genesis 1:1–10 on 24 December 1968

title: The Blue Marble
caption: The Blue Marble — the whole Earth seen from Apollo 17, set entirely in the words of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
source: Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948), full text, United Nations

title: The Starry Night
caption: Van Gogh's Starry Night, drawn entirely from the opening of Walt Whitman's Song of Myself.
source: Walt Whitman, Song of Myself (Leaves of Grass, Project Gutenberg eBook #1322), opening sections, public domain

title: The Great Wave
caption: Hokusai's Great Wave off Kanagawa, drawn entirely from the opening chapters of Melville's Moby-Dick.
source: Herman Melville, Moby-Dick (1851), chapters 1–2, public domain

title: Cooper Institute
caption: A portrait of Abraham Lincoln, set entirely in the words of the Cooper Institute address that helped carry him to the presidency.
source: Abraham Lincoln, Address at Cooper Institute, New York, 27 February 1860, as printed in Speeches & Letters of Abraham Lincoln (1907), public domain

title: La Gioconda
caption: Leonardo's Mona Lisa, drawn entirely from Walter Pater's celebrated essay on Leonardo da Vinci.
source: Walter Pater, The Renaissance (1873), essay on Leonardo da Vinci up to the Mona Lisa passage, public domain

title: Endless forms
caption: Charles Darwin, drawn entirely from the last page of On the Origin of Species — “endless forms most beautiful.”
source: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1859), end of the final chapter, public domain

title: The Star
caption: The Pillars of Creation, drawn entirely from H. G. Wells's 1897 story The Star.
source: H. G. Wells, The Star (1897), the complete story, from Tales of Space and Time (Project Gutenberg eBook #27365), public domain

title: The Wanderer
caption: Caspar David Friedrich's Wanderer above the Sea of Fog, drawn entirely from the Prologue of Nietzsche's Thus Spake Zarathustra.
source: Friedrich Nietzsche, Thus Spake Zarathustra (1883), Zarathustra's Prologue, translated by Thomas Common (Project Gutenberg eBook #1998), public domain

title: Fuji-no-Yama
caption: Hokusai's Red Fuji, drawn entirely from Lafcadio Hearn's essay Fuji-no-Yama.
source: Lafcadio Hearn, Fuji-no-Yama, in Exotics and Retrospectives (1898), the essay after its epigraph (Project Gutenberg eBook #42735), public domain

title: Learning to Read
caption: Frederick Douglass, drawn entirely from the chapters of his Narrative in which he teaches himself to read.
source: Frederick Douglass, Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave (1845), chapters V–VIII (Project Gutenberg eBook #23), public domain

title: The Boys' Ambition
caption: Mark Twain, drawn entirely from the steamboat-dreaming chapters of Life on the Mississippi.
source: Mark Twain, Life on the Mississippi (1883), chapters 4–6 (Project Gutenberg eBook #245), public domain

title: The House of Usher
caption: Edgar Allan Poe, drawn entirely from his tale The Fall of the House of Usher.
source: Edgar Allan Poe, The Fall of the House of Usher (1839), from the second paragraph to the end (Project Gutenberg eBook #932), public domain

title: My Inventions
caption: Nikola Tesla, drawn entirely from his own memoir My Inventions.
source: Nikola Tesla, My Inventions (Electrical Experimenter, 1919), chapter III, My Later Endeavors (Wikisource, My Inventions, revision 15728285), public domain

title: Preliminary Discourse
caption: John Herschel, drawn entirely from his Preliminary Discourse on the Study of Natural Philosophy.
source: John F. W. Herschel, A Preliminary Discourse on the Study of Natural Philosophy (1831), §§ 77–101 (Project Gutenberg eBook #54897), public domain
